findings.description: The truthiness check `if fg:` (and likewise `if bg:` at line 684) drops color index 0, so a valid 256-color value of 0 is silently ignored instead of emitting an ANSI code.
findings.rationale: Trigger: style("text", fg=0) or bg=0. Previously `fg is not None` emitted "\033[38;5;0m". Now 0 is falsy, so no color code is emitted and the text renders in the default color. The mechanism is the falsy test replacing an explicit None check, and the impact is silently wrong terminal output for black (index 0).

findings.description: The 0..255 range check for integer colors was removed, and bools are now accepted as ints, so out-of-range values produce malformed escape codes.
findings.rationale: Trigger: style("x", fg=256) or fg=True. Previously these raised an error. Now the function emits "38;5;256" or "38;5;1". The mechanism is that the int branch no longer validates its range or excludes bool, and the impact is an invalid or unexpected escape sequence that terminals ignore or misrender instead of a clear error.
